status: Exploratory pilot protocol written before this experiment, after earlier different pilots; not preregistered
question: Does increasing the mean separation of an independent informative feature Z reduce recovery of the fixed correlation-only pair X,Y in explanation rankings?
design: Given group labels, not learned clusters; isolates interpretation as in the motivation paper
pairing: Exactly same observations/noise, labels, seeds and test anchors across delta; only Z means change
primary: Probability both planted feature indices are among the top 3; Wilson 95% intervals over independent datasets
methods: RF permutation negative log-loss importance (saturation diagnostic)
LIME absolute weights averaged over 8 balanced heldout objects
PCA absolute first-PC loadings after pooled standardization
PCA first-PC loadings averaged over separately centered and standardized groups (mean-invariance control)
Direct Fisher-z correlation-difference scores; feature score is maximum incident-pair score
negative_control: rho_A=rho_B=0, 20 independent datasets, delta 0 and 4; Holm FWER at 0.05 for 45 fixed-label pair comparisons
limitations: Feature recovery is not pair relationship/sign recovery
Z is a valid predictor, not irrelevant noise
Univariate rankings, local LIME and PCA solve different tasks
No claim of new method or novelty established
No control of learned-partition selection bias in this fixed-label experiment
